content_voiceover: This table defines the plasma cell dyscrasia spectrum for boards. MGUS requires a serum M protein under three grams per deciliter, bone marrow plasma cells under ten percent, and no myeloma defining events, with about a one percent per year progression risk. Smoldering multiple myeloma has a higher M protein, three grams per deciliter or more, or urine M protein of five hundred milligrams a day or more, with ten to sixty percent bone marrow plasma cells, still asymptomatic, but a ten percent per year progression risk in the first five years. Symptomatic multiple myeloma requires clonal bone marrow plasma cells of ten percent or higher, or a biopsy proven plasmacytoma, plus a myeloma defining event, either a CRAB feature such as hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, or lytic bone lesions, or a SLiM biomarker like sixty percent bone marrow plasma cells, an involved to uninvolved free light chain ratio of one hundred or more, or more than one MRI lesion. Solitary plasmacytoma and plasma cell leukemia, defined by five percent or more circulating plasma cells, round out the spectrum.
keypoints: MGUS: M protein under 3 g/dL, BM plasma cells under 10%, no myeloma defining events, about 1%/year progression
Smoldering myeloma: M protein 3 g/dL or more or urine 500 mg/day or more, BM plasma cells 10-60%, about 10%/year progression
Symptomatic myeloma: clonal BM plasma cells 10% or more, or plasmacytoma, plus a CRAB feature or SLiM biomarker
SLiM biomarkers: 60% or more BM plasma cells, free light chain ratio 100 or more, or more than one MRI lesion 5mm or larger
Plasma cell leukemia: 5% or more circulating plasma cells
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the boards shorthand. MGUS is under three grams M protein and under ten percent marrow plasma cells with no organ damage. Smoldering myeloma bridges the gap with higher counts but still no CRAB features. Symptomatic myeloma needs a CRAB feature or a SLiM biomarker, sixty percent plasma cells, a free light chain ratio over one hundred, or more than one MRI lesion. Plasma cell leukemia means five percent or more circulating plasma cells.
